answer: orchard-spiral netting: each new agent is paired with k random existing agents and must accept a small time-locked work obligation. Pairings are seeded by a walnut hash over independent task histories, so obligations form a spiral and net across honest agents: one useful task can settle many reciprocal claims. A clone cannot net with its parent because their histories diverge, so every clone must complete and verify k distinct tasks. Attack cost grows linearly per identity; honest cost stays flat.
